test_title: PYST 16: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 21 Jun 2024 Shift 4)
subject: maths
question: A train starts from station P with 'n' number of passengers. At station Q, 20% of the passengers get down and 50 passengers get in. At station R, 40% of the passengers get down and 10 passengers get in. If a total of 520 passengers are left on the train, find the value of 'n'.
solution:
**Given:**

Initial number of passengers at station P = n

At station Q, 20% of the passengers get down and 50 passengers get in.

At station R, 40% of the passengers get down and 10 passengers get in.

Final number of passengers = 520

**Formula Used:**

Passengers at any station = Initial passengers - Passengers who got down + Passengers who got in

**Calculation:**

Passengers at station Q:

Passengers who got down at Q = 20% of n = 0.2n

Passengers who got in at Q = 50

Passengers at Q = n - 0.2n + 50

Passengers at Q = 0.8n + 50

Passengers at station R:

Passengers who got down at R = 40% of passengers at Q = 0.4(0.8n + 50)

Passengers who got in at R = 10

Passengers at R = (0.8n + 50) - 0.4(0.8n + 50) + 10

Solving for passengers at R:

Passengers at R = (0.8n + 50) - (0.32n + 20) + 10

Passengers at R = 0.8n + 50 - 0.32n - 20 + 10

Passengers at R = 0.48n + 40

Given that passengers at R = 520

⇒ 0.48n + 40 = 520

⇒ 0.48n = 520 - 40

⇒ 0.48n = 480

⇒ n = 480 / 0.48

⇒ n = 1000

**The value of 'n' is 1000.**
